title: High-titer convalescent serum from cats recovered from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome protects SFTSV-infected mice.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of vaccines or antiviral drugs for feline SFTS by investigating whether convalescent sera from cats that had recovered from SFTS could be used for passive immunotherapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved measuring neutralizing antibody titers in convalescent sera from six human SFTS survivors and 14 cats that had recovered from naturally acquired SFTS, and evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of these sera in SFTSV-infected, interferon receptor-deficient AG129 mice.
analysis.methods: The researchers used 80% plaque-reduction neutralization test (PRNT 80) to measure neutralizing antibody titers and evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of convalescent cat serum in SFTSV-infected mice.
analysis.main_results: Some SFTS-recovered cats exhibited high PRNT 80 titers, and passive administration of high-titer convalescent cat serum early after infection protected SFTSV-infected mice, with a single dose given at 2 or 3 days post-infection completely protecting mice, whereas treatment at 4 days post-infection resulted in 40% survival.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that some SFTS-recovered cats can develop high neutralizing antibody titers and that their sera can exert therapeutic effects in an SFTSV-infected mouse model, supporting further evaluation of passive immunotherapy as a treatment strategy for feline SFTS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that convalescent cat sera could be used for passive immunotherapy to treat feline SFTS, which could have implications for the development of therapeutic strategies for this disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small sample size and the use of a mouse model, which may not fully represent the complexity of the disease in cats. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of convalescent cat sera for passive immunotherapy in SFTSV-infected mice. Some SFTS-recovered cats had high neutralizing antibody titers, and early administration of their sera protected mice, supporting further investigation of this approach for feline SFTS treatment.

title: Demographic decomposition of changes in notifications of Japanese spotted fever, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and scrub typhus in Japan, 2014-2016 versus 2022-2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to understand the factors contributing to the increase in notifications of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in Japan between 2014-2016 and 2022-2024, as part of a broader context of rising tick- and mite-borne infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a decomposition approach to analyze changes in notifications over two time periods, focusing on Japan's population dynamics and age-specific trends for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, Japanese spotted fever, and scrub typhus.
analysis.methods: The study decomposed the change in average annual notifications into three components: national population size, age composition across published age classes, and age-class-specific notification rates, using a consistent methodology for all three diseases.
analysis.main_results: The decomposition results are presented in cases per year and per 100 baseline cases, alongside various scenarios including a fixed-rate standardised scenario, an eight-region four-factor decomposition, sex-specific analyses, and a supplementary Poisson interval.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as standardisation quantities rather than causal effects, highlighting the methodological approach to understanding demographic contributions to disease notification trends.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into how demographic changes may influence the notification patterns of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, aiding in the development of targeted surveillance and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies solely on published aggregate statistics and does not claim causality, which limits the strength of the evidence to a moderate level.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the factors contributing to the increase in notifications of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in Japan between 2014-2016 and 2022-2024. It decomposes the change in notifications into three components: national population size, age composition, and age-class-specific notification rates. The results are presented in cases per year and per 100 baseline cases, alongside various scenarios. The authors interpret the findings as standardisation quantities, not causal effects, and note that only published aggregate statistics are used. The study provides insights into demographic influences on disease notification trends, which can inform public health strategies. However, the reliance on aggregate data limits the evidence strength to moderate. The methodology is consistent across all three diseases studied, and the analysis is based on a fixed protocol.

title: Clinical Management Strategy for a Severe Case of Novel Bunyavirus Infection Complicated by Invasive Aspergillosis in an Elderly Patient

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an acute infectious disease caused by SFTSV, representing an emerging tick-borne disease. Complications such as encephalopathy and secondary invasive fungal infections significantly increase the mortality rate of this disease, for which no specific antiviral therapeutics are currently approved.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Case Report: A 70-year-old male patient presented with persistent fever, thrombocytopenia and bleeding tendencies following a tick bite. His condition deteriorated rapidly, characterized by convulsions, cognitive impairment and multiple organ dysfunction, leading to a confirmed diagnosis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by secondary invasive aspergillosis.
analysis.methods: The patient’s life was successfully saved through a comprehensive clinical regimen, including early antiviral therapy with favipiravir, broad-spectrum anti-infective treatment, targeted antifungal therapy against Aspergillus with voriconazole, anti-inflammatory intervention with low-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, immune modulation using intravenous immunoglobulin, multiple sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange, liver protection, acid suppression, hemostasis and precise anticoagulation guided by dynamic risk assessments of hemorrhage and thrombosis.
analysis.main_results: Following these multimodal interventions, the patient was smoothly weaned from mechanical ventilation and successfully extubated. His clinical indicators, viral load and inflammatory markers progressively declined alongside the recovery of organ function, ultimately resulting in a successful discharge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This rare case of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by invasive aspergillosis highlights two key priorities in the management of critically ill older patients: close monitoring for neurological complications and secondary fungal infections, together with a multidimensional therapeutic approach incorporating antiviral therapy, plasma exchange for immunomodulation and targeted antifungal treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the importance of multidimensional therapeutic approaches for managing severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in elderly patients, particularly those at risk for secondary fungal infections.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 70-year-old male patient with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) complicated by invasive aspergillosis. The patient presented with persistent fever, thrombocytopenia, and bleeding tendencies following a tick bite, and his condition rapidly deteriorated with convulsions, cognitive impairment, and multiple organ dysfunction. The study highlights the importance of close monitoring for neurological complications and secondary fungal infections in elderly patients with SFTS. A comprehensive clinical regimen, including early antiviral therapy with favipiravir, broad-spectrum anti-infective treatment, targeted antifungal therapy with voriconazole, anti-inflammatory intervention with low-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, immune modulation using intravenous immunoglobulin, therapeutic plasma exchange, liver protection, acid suppression, hemostasis, and precise anticoagulation guided by dynamic risk assessments, was employed. The patient was successfully extubated and discharged after his clinical indicators, viral load, and inflammatory markers declined alongside recovery of organ function. The case underscores the need for a multidimensional therapeutic approach in managing severe SFTS, particularly in older patients at risk for secondary fungal infections. The study is a single case report and does not provide statistical or comparative data, limiting its generalizability.

title: Inhibitory activity and mechanism of a scorpion-derived peptide BmKDfsin3 against SFTSV and HSV-1

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the antiviral potential of scorpion-derived peptides against SFTSV and HSV-1, addressing the need for broad-spectrum, low-toxicity antiviral agents in viral prevention and treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the inhibitory activity of the scorpion venom peptide BmKDfsin3 against SFTSV and HSV-1 in A549 cells, conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on viral replication inhibition.
analysis.methods: Antiviral phase assays were performed to evaluate the effect of BmKDfsin3 on viral replication stages, and the activation of p38 and transcription factors p52 and IRF3 was assessed to understand the mechanism of action.
analysis.main_results: BmKDfsin3 concentration-dependently inhibited SFTSV and HSV-1 replication in A549 cells, primarily targeting the post-entry stage of the viral life cycle. It also suppressed p38 activation and enhanced type I and III interferon signaling pathways.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that BmKDfsin3 acts through a dual mechanism, inhibiting viral replication while promoting host immune responses, which is a novel approach for broad-spectrum antiviral activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that BmKDfsin3 could be a promising candidate for developing antiviral therapies with broad application against both RNA and DNA viruses, including SFTSV and HSV-1.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro experiments, and the evidence for antiviral activity is strong based on direct observations, though in vivo validation is needed to confirm its therapeutic potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral activity of the scorpion-derived peptide BmKDfsin3 against SFTSV and HSV-1. The research highlights the need for broad-spectrum antiviral agents with low toxicity. The study design involved in vitro experiments using A549 cells to assess the peptide's effects on viral replication. Results showed that BmKDfsin3 concentration-dependently inhibited SFTSV and HSV-1 replication, primarily targeting the post-entry stage of their life cycles. Mechanistically, the peptide suppressed p38 activation and enhanced interferon signaling by activating p52 and IRF3. The findings suggest a dual mechanism of action, offering new insights into antiviral peptide design. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform the development of effective antiviral therapies. However, the evidence is limited to in vitro results, and further in vivo studies are necessary to validate these findings.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Available data indicate that SFTSV exposure and infection occur across a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a simple single-reservoir interpretation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Domestic ruminants frequently exhibit high seroprevalence and may function as sentinels of enzootic activity, while occasional virus isolation from cattle demonstrates that viable virus can be recovered from naturally infected livestock, although this does not establish reservoir or amplification competence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review underscores the need for One Health surveillance that incorporates clinical data from companion animals and applies evidence‐based interpretation to improve recognition of animal–human interfaces associated with potential spillover risk.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the epidemiology and spillover risk of Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in animals across East Asia. The study focuses on the host range, geographic distribution, and diagnostic methods for SFTSV infection in domestic livestock, companion animals, wildlife, and captive species. The findings suggest that SFTSV has a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a single-reservoir model. While domestic ruminants show high seroprevalence and may act as sentinels for enzootic activity, the role of these animals in viral maintenance and amplification remains unclear. The review highlights the importance of integrating animal infection data into an ecological framework and emphasizes the need for One Health surveillance to better understand and mitigate spillover risks from animal to human populations.

title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the integrated proteomic and metabolomic mechanisms underlying mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients, as SFTS remains a poorly understood public health threat with high mortality rates in severe cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective cohort study was conducted on ICU-admitted patients with severe SFTS between July 2019 and October 2023, dividing them into survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups based on 28-day clinical outcomes.
analysis.methods: Baseline demographic and clinical data were collected from electronic medical records, and laboratory parameters such as viral load, lactate, and other indicators were measured within 24 h of ICU admission. Specimens were collected in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Yantai Qishan Hospital, and the study was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Yantai Qishan Hospital.
analysis.main_results: No statistically significant differences were observed in demographic characteristics or most comorbidities between the survivor and non-survivor groups (all P > 0.05). However, the non-survivor group had significantly lower median GCS (9.0 vs. 11.0, P = 0.002), higher median viral RNA copy number (1,150,000 vs. 1,000,000, P < 0.05), and elevated levels of lactate, PCT, IL-6, and ferritin (all P < 0.05). Additionally, the non-survivor group showed higher levels of liver, renal, and myocardial injury markers (all P < 0.05) and prolonged coagulation parameters with reduced FIB and elevated D-dimer levels (all P < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism in non-survivors, with decreased L-tryptophan and increased kynurenine pathway metabolites, suggesting a potential link between metabolic disturbances and adverse outcomes in SFTS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for SFTS, particularly in identifying metabolic biomarkers associated with mortality in critically ill patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a limited sample size and potential confounding factors, such as co-infections and immunocompromised status, which were excluded. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the focus on observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the proteomic and metabolomic profiles of ICU-admitted SFTS patients to identify mechanisms associated with mortality. A prospective cohort design was used, with patients divided into survivor and non-survivor groups based on 28-day outcomes. The study collected clinical data and laboratory parameters, including GCS scores, viral load, and inflammatory markers. Results showed no significant differences in demographics or comorbidities but highlighted more severe clinical and laboratory features in non-survivors. Metabolomic profiling revealed significant tryptophan metabolic disturbances, with decreased L-tryptophan and increased kynurenine pathway metabolites in non-survivors. These findings suggest a potential role for metabolic biomarkers in predicting mortality in SFTS. The study's limitations include a small sample size and exclusion of certain confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.
